=You are an expert technical recruiter specializing in Business Analyst, Product Owner, Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer, Business Intelligence, Snowflake, AI Automation, and Data Platform roles.

Evaluate a batch of job postings against the candidate's profile. This is a SCORING-ONLY pass -- do not write any resume content, only judge fit.

CANDIDATE SKILLS & POSITIONING:

{{ JSON.stringify({ core_positioning: $json.body.master_resume.core_positioning, skills_keyword_bank: $json.body.master_resume.skills_keyword_bank }) }}

JOB POSTINGS:

{{ JSON.stringify($json.body.jobs.map(j => ({...j, description: (j.description || "").slice(0, 4000)}))) }}

TASK:

Evaluate every job posting against the candidate profile. Return ONE object per job.

CANDIDATE'S ACTUAL EXPERIENCE LEVEL:

The candidate has approximately 5.5 years of professional work experience (2.5 years at Allegis Group as a Business Analyst II, roughly 2 years at KPMG as an Analyst, plus a 2-year Master's degree counted toward professional-level experience), plus a short internship at Thrivent. The candidate is transitioning FROM business analyst/BA-adjacent roles INTO analytics engineering -- they are NOT a senior or staff-level analytics/data engineer with 6+ years of hands-on data engineering experience, and scoring must reflect that honestly.

STEP 1 -- Determine the role's required experience level.

Read the job description for explicit years-of-experience language ("5+ years", "8-10 years", "minimum 6 years of experience"). If no explicit number is stated, infer from title and seniority language instead:
- Staff / Principal / Director / Head of / VP -> treat as requiring 8+ years
- Senior / Sr. / Lead -> treat as requiring 6-7 years
- Mid-level / Analytics Engineer / Analyst II / no seniority modifier -> treat as requiring 2-5 years
- Associate / Analyst I / Junior / Entry-level -> treat as requiring 0-2 years

STEP 2 -- Apply a MANDATORY experience-gap penalty to match_score, before finalizing the score. This is a hard deduction, not a suggestion -- apply it even when the candidate's skills otherwise match well, because a real hiring filter (ATS or recruiter) will screen out an experience-level mismatch regardless of skill overlap:
- Required experience 0-5 years: no penalty (candidate is at ~5.5 years)
- Required experience 6-7 years: subtract 15 points
- Required experience 8-9 years: subtract 30 points
- Required experience 10+ years: subtract 45 points

STEP 3 -- Score the skill/domain fit using the tightened anchors below, THEN apply the Step 2 penalty on top of that base score. The final match_score is the post-penalty number.

Scoring Guidance (tightened -- be strict, most postings should NOT land in the 80s/90s):

90-100 = Exceptional fit: required experience is within reach (<=4 years) AND deep, direct overlap on core tools/domain (Snowflake, SQL, analytics engineering, BA/data platform work)
75-89 = Strong fit: good skill overlap, experience requirement roughly matches or is only slightly above candidate's level
60-74 = Good fit: real overlap but a noticeable gap in either skills or experience level
45-59 = Reasonable fit: partial overlap, meaningful gap in skills or experience (this should be a common, not rare, bucket for a large batch)
30-44 = Weak fit: minor overlap only
Below 30 = Poor fit, will be auto-dropped

Do not let scores cluster in the 80s-90s by default. Across a large batch of varied postings, the DISTRIBUTION should be wide -- most jobs should fall in the 40-75 range, with 85+ reserved for genuinely excellent, low-experience-gap matches. If nearly every job in a batch scores 80+, you are scoring too generously and must re-calibrate lower.

Favor jobs involving:

- Business Analysis
- Product Ownership
- Analytics Engineering
- Data Engineering
- Snowflake
- SQL
- Tableau
- AI Automation
- Data Platforms
- Process Improvement
- Business Process Optimization
- Stakeholder Management

Reduce scores for:

- Heavy software engineering roles
- Deep infrastructure roles
- Non-data technical positions
- Manufacturing automation roles
- PLC engineering roles
- Embedded systems roles

RETURN ONLY VALID JSON.

DO NOT RETURN:

- Markdown
- Explanations
- Introductory text
- Code fences

Required Output Format:

[
  {
    "job_id": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "location": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "match_score": 85,
    "tech_stack": [
      "Python",
      "SQL"
    ],
    "missing_skills": [
      "Airflow"
    ],
    "pitch": "Short explanation of fit."
  }
]

Rules:

- Return exactly one object per input job.
- Preserve job_id, title, company, location, and url exactly as received.
- match_score must be numeric.
- tech_stack must always be an array.
- missing_skills must always be an array.
- pitch should be brief and actionable.
- Return only valid JSON.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ (() => { const cl = $('Extract cover letter').all().map(i => i.json); const clIds = new Set(cl.map(x => x.job_id)); const rest = $('Merge tailored').all().map(i => i.json).filter(x => !clIds.has(x.job_id)).map(x => Object.assign({}, x, { cover_letter: "" })); return { success: true, results: cl.concat(rest) }; })() }}

=You are writing a personalized cover letter for Gurkirat Singh Wadhawan, applying to the {{ $json.title }} role at {{ $json.company }} ({{ $json.location }}).

CANDIDATE RESUME:
GURKIRAT SINGH WADHAWAN
Analytics Engineer | Snowflake | SQL | Python | AI Automation

WORK EXPERIENCE
Allegis Group — Business Analyst II, Treasury (February 2024 – Present)
Employee of the Year and Rising Star Award recipient.
- Reduced procurement review preparation effort by 80% by designing an AI-ready procurement intelligence platform using Python, SQL, Snowflake, and deployment automation.
- Built AI-powered analytics solutions using Snowflake Cortex Analyst, semantic models, SQL, and natural language querying.
- Developed a centralized contract intelligence repository using Snowflake and Python.
- Delivered AI and GenAI training to 300+ employees.
- Built enterprise Tableau dashboards that uncovered $9M+ in savings opportunities.
- Developed a unified corporate card spend analysis platform integrating more than 10 million records.
- Created enterprise data products using Snowflake, SQL, Tableau, and reporting pipelines.

Thrivent Federal Credit Union — Business Management Analyst Intern
- Led operational efficiency review and process optimization initiatives.

KPMG — Analyst, IT Consulting
- Developed cloud transformation strategies.
- Performed business process assessments and ITIL gap analyses.
- Created executive-level technology roadmaps.
- Worked with financial services and manufacturing clients.

EDUCATION
Master of Science in Information Systems, University of Maryland, Robert H. Smith School of Business
Bachelor of Engineering, Electronics, Mumbai University

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming: Python, SQL, R
Data: Snowflake, Data Modeling, Semantic Models, Data Pipelines, ETL
Analytics: Tableau, Power BI, Executive Dashboards
AI: Snowflake Cortex, OpenAI APIs, LLM Applications, AI Automation, Prompt Engineering

WHY THIS ROLE IS A STRONG MATCH (from prior analysis):
{{ $json.pitch }}

RELEVANT TECH STACK FOR THIS ROLE:
{{ $json.tech_stack }}

SKILLS THE ROLE WANTS THAT AREN'T ON THE RESUME (do not claim these, address them only if it strengthens the letter honestly, e.g. framing as fast learner with adjacent experience):
{{ $json.missing_skills }}

TASK:
Write a 280-350 word cover letter for this specific role. Requirements:
- Open with a specific, concrete hook tied to something real about {{ $json.company }} or the role itself — never "I am writing to express my interest."
- Reference 2-3 specific things from the resume (real project names, tools, outcomes) and connect them directly to what this role needs, using the tech stack and pitch above.
- Match tone to the role: professional but not stiff, confident but not overblown.
- Close with a specific, low-friction call to action, not "I look forward to hearing from you."
- Do not invent facts, metrics, or experience not present in the resume above.
- Output only the letter body — no subject line, no "Dear Hiring Manager" placeholder, no explanation of what you wrote.
